user_stories.title: Implement Siamese Network for Bid/Ask Symmetric Features
user_stories.description: Create a PyTorch module that uses a Siamese architecture with shared weights to extract symmetric spatial features from bid and ask data in the limit order book.
acceptance_criteria: Module takes two inputs: bid_data and ask_data of shape [batch, time, features].
Outputs a fused feature vector of fixed dimension.
Shared convolutional or linear layers are used for symmetry.
user_stories.verification: python -c "import sys, torch; sys.path.insert(0, 'src/models'); from siamese import SiameseNetwork; net = SiameseNetwork(input_dim=5, hidden_dim=32); bid = torch.randn(2, 10, 5); ask = torch.randn(2, 10, 5); out = net(bid, ask); print(out.shape)"

user_stories.title: Implement Feature Fusion Layer for Macroeconomic Data
user_stories.description: Create a layer that fuses the output from the Siamese network with additional macroeconomic features.
acceptance_criteria: Layer takes two inputs: siamese_features and macro_features.
Outputs a combined feature sequence ready for temporal processing.
Fusion method is configurable (e.g., concatenation, attention).
user_stories.verification: python -c "import sys, torch; sys.path.insert(0, 'src/models'); from fusion import FeatureFusion; fusion = FeatureFusion(siamese_dim=32, macro_dim=8, output_dim=40); siamese = torch.randn(2, 10, 32); macro = torch.randn(2, 10, 8); out = fusion(siamese, macro); print(out.shape)"

user_stories.title: Integrate T-KAN Orchestrator Head
user_stories.description: Use the existing T-KAN implementation to create a head that processes the fused feature sequence. It MUST output exactly 2 features for the targets.
acceptance_criteria: Head takes the fused sequence and outputs predictions for exactly 2 targets.
Utilizes the T-KAN layer from src/models/t_kan.py.
Output shape at the feature dimension must be exactly 2.
user_stories.verification: python -c "import sys, torch; sys.path.insert(0, 'src/models'); from t_kan_heads import TKANHead; head = TKANHead(input_dim=40, hidden_dims=[64, 32], output_dim=2); x = torch.randn(2, 10, 40); out = head(x); assert out.shape[-1] == 2, f'Expected 2, got {out.shape[-1]}'; print(out.shape)"

user_stories.title: Integrate DAIN Layer for Temporal Causality
user_stories.description: Implement Deep Adaptive Input Normalization (DAIN) to enforce temporal causality in the input data.
acceptance_criteria: DAIN layer normalizes inputs adaptively over time.
Ensures no future information leakage in normalization.
Compatible with sequence data of variable length.
user_stories.verification: python -c "import sys, torch; sys.path.insert(0, 'src/data'); from normalization import DAIN; dain = DAIN(input_dim=10); x = torch.randn(2, 10, 10); out = dain(x); print(out.shape); print('DAIN applied successfully')"

user_stories.title: Assemble Full Causal LOB Forecaster Model
user_stories.description: Combine Siamese network, feature fusion, DAIN, and T-KAN head into a single PyTorch model. The model must output shape (batch, seq_len, 2).
acceptance_criteria: Model takes bid_data, ask_data, and macro_data as inputs.
Applies DAIN for normalization, Siamese for features, fusion, and T-KAN for predictions.
Output dimension is STRICTLY 2 (for t0 and t1).
Model is causal, i.e., predictions at time t depend only on data up to t.
user_stories.verification: python -c "import sys, torch; sys.path.insert(0, 'src/models'); from causal_lob_forecaster import CausalLOBForecaster; model = CausalLOBForecaster(bid_ask_dim=5, macro_dim=8, hidden_dims=[32, 64], output_dim=2); bid = torch.randn(2, 1000, 5); ask = torch.randn(2, 1000, 5); macro = torch.randn(2, 1000, 8); out = model(bid, ask, macro); print(out.shape); assert out.shape[-1] == 2, 'Output feature dimension must be exactly 2'"

user_stories.title: Update Model Registry and Training Configuration
user_stories.description: Register the new CausalLOBForecaster model in the model registry and update the training script to support it with output_dim=2.
acceptance_criteria: Model is added to src/models/registry.py with a unique name.
train.py can instantiate and train the model using config parameters.
Training configuration initializes the model to output exactly 2 features.
user_stories.verification: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'src/models'); from registry import get_model; model = get_model('causal_lob_forecaster', input_dim=40, output_dim=2); print('Model retrieved successfully')"

user_stories.title: Create Basic Tests for Causal LOB Forecaster
user_stories.description: Write pytest tests to verify the functionality of the new model and its components, explicitly testing for the correct output shape.
acceptance_criteria: Test file exists and can be run with pytest.
Tests cover model instantiation, forward pass, and causality enforcement.
Tests assert that the output shape is (batch, seq_len, 2).
